models_evaluated: single base LLM with five prompt-defined sensitivity variants

links.outcome: Missed crisis escalations (false negatives) versus false positives across sensitivity thresholds against clinician consensus
links.effect: False-negative rate fell monotonically from 87% to 0% as sensitivity rose; high and extreme variants reached 98.9% and 100% recall, with false-positive rates rising accordingly.
links.quote: As sensitivity increased, the false-negative rate decreased monotonically from 87% to 0%, while false-positive rates rose accordingly.

links.outcome: Real-time detection of suicide and crisis risk in chatbot conversation turns, including latency
links.effect: High and extreme-sensitivity variants achieved 98.9% and 100% recall with mean latency <1 s, showing real-time per-turn detection is feasible.
links.quote: High - and  extreme-sensitivity variants achieved near-perfect (98.9%) and perfect (100%) recall, demonstrating that near–zero–miss crisis detection from natural language is technically feasible in real time (mean latency <1 s).
